public_rationale: Independent reporting confirms that Marcus praised coding autocomplete before this post. That supports the substance of his self-description. It does not establish 'invariably', and no complete counterexample was verified. Calling the claim supported would silently weaken its frequency commitment; calling it contradicted would require a documented exception.

our_interpretation: This is a claim about Marcus's public communication, not an independent claim that coding tools improve productivity.
The plain reading is that his discussions identifying positive generative AI uses consistently include coding assistance as useful autocomplete.
The relevant period is his public record through publication. This retrospective description of a speaking habit has no stated starting date and is not tied to a reporting quarter.
A discussion is assessed in context, rather than treating every isolated sentence as a separate occasion. Equivalent descriptions of coding assistance can count without the exact word 'autocomplete'.
'Kind of' qualifies the description of the tool; it does not remove the checkable commitment in 'invariably'.
criteria.support_condition: A sufficiently comprehensive, independently documented record of his relevant public discussions consistently includes useful coding autocomplete.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A complete, dated public discussion before publication identifies positive generative AI uses but omits coding assistance, with enough context to rule out editorial omission.
